# Logo permission request email template

Copy into a private draft and replace every bracketed placeholder. Verify the
recipient through the rights holder's official site and check existing terms
first using the [operator workflow](../logo-rights-workflow.md). Send only after
operator review and authorization. Keep the completed email and reply outside
the repository. Do not attach an image unless copying is already covered;
identify it through an official source link instead.

The draft assumes one operator's private, unshared calendar. Correct statements
that do not match the actual use. List multiple assets only if the recipient
controls the relevant rights. This request neither accepts fees or terms nor
establishes approval.

## Subject

Permission or clarification request: private calendar use of [exact logo]

## Email body

Dear [rights holder's licensing or brand team],

I operate a personal instance of SMART Sports Calendar, an open-source,
self-hosted application that synchronizes sports fixtures into my own
Microsoft 365/Outlook calendar. I would like to clarify whether your existing
terms cover the use below or, if necessary, request permission.

The exact image(s) I would like to use are:

- [Asset name, variant/version and official source page]

The intended use is strictly private and non-commercial, by me in
[country/territory], for [requested period]. The calendar would not be shared
with other users or made publicly accessible. There would be no advertising,
sale of the image or suggestion of endorsement by your organization.

The application would store the image on my private server and upload separate
inline copies to my Microsoft 365/Outlook calendar events. Microsoft would
therefore store the image within my account, and I would view the events on my
personal devices. Private backups would include the image and could restore
it within the permitted period and scope.

The current processing accepts PNG or JPEG, removes embedded metadata,
preserves aspect ratio, centres the image on a transparent 60 x 60 pixel
canvas and converts it to PNG. It is displayed at up to 30 x 30 pixels within
each relevant calendar event. I would not otherwise alter the design.

Although the application's source code is public, your image would not be
included in its public repository, container images, releases, documentation
or public screenshots. This request is solely for my described personal use;
it does not seek redistribution rights for other users of the application.

Could you please confirm:

1. Whether existing terms cover all these uses, with a reference to the
   applicable terms, or whether you can grant permission for this scope.
2. Whether copying, backup and the described technical transformations are
   permitted, including removal of embedded metadata.
3. Any attribution wording and placement, copyright or trademark notices,
   and brand restrictions.
4. Any territorial or time limits, renewal requirements, revocation conditions,
   and requirements for removing stored copies or backups.
5. Whether any fee, additional agreement or other condition would apply.
6. Which official file or permitted download channel I should use if approved.

If you do not control the relevant rights, please direct me to the responsible
rights holder or licensing contact. I will keep the image disabled until the
necessary coverage is established and use a text-only calendar meanwhile.

Thank you for considering my request.

Kind regards,

[Operator name]

[Reply email address]
